answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks with quadratic bonding: registering identities costs a deposit that grows with the square of how many one operator already holds. Spawning a second sybil costs four times the first; a thousandth costs a million times more. A lone honest agent in a quiet oasis garden pays almost nothing, but a delta-flood of fake identities becomes economically impossible to sustain, since every bonded account risks forfeit if it grades dishonestly.
